text:
maria: Quick callout — noticed a perf regression hitting our MQA paged-KV codepath on p4d instances. Throughput down ~30% for seqlen=1024 when KV block_size=256 vs 512. nvprof shows a lot of time in a generic attention kernel after layer ~16. Anyone else see this?

ajit: Saw similar yesterday on a 8xA100 test. Repro steps: switch model to mqa-4x, set paged_kv.block=256, run perf harness at batch=8, seq=1024. Peak tokens/s dropped. I have flamegraphs (link: https://internal.perf/redwood/fg/2145).

maria: thanks — attaching small profile snippet: `attn_gqa_paged::kernel_select -> fallback: attn_generic` at ~50% of attention time. Also cache layout shows more TLB misses when block=256.

zach: This smells like kernel selector thresholds that are sequence-length aware but not KV-block aware. Our selector currently uses {seqlen, head_dim, mqa_factor} but not `kv_block_bytes`. We should feed blocksize and page-miss rate into the scoring.

neha: Also batching: small micro-batches (batch=2 -> internal batching to 32) end up picking a different exec path. If KV page prefetch isn't primed, first N tokens hit page faults and push us to generic kernel due to poor latency estimates. Try `runtime.flags.prefetch_on_alloc=true` for a quick test.

ajit: Quick experiment results: enabling prefetch_on_alloc -> +18% throughput at block=256, seq=1024, batch=8. Still ~10% below block=512 baseline. Logs: `page_faults: 120 -> 8`, `attn_generic_time: 420ms -> 120ms`.

zach: Propose we update autotuner to consider a third axis: kv_layout_hash = f(block_size, page_size, mapping). Then during sampling we run short probes at representative seqlen buckets (<=128, 256-512, 1024-2048) and pick kernel per-bucket. That should avoid global fallback for mixed workloads.

maria: Sounds good. Two quick asks: 1) can someone add block_size into the selector feature vector? 2) run a small probe sweep on p4d with seqlen=512 and 1024 to collect metrics.

neha: I'll add the probe harness changes — will emit metrics: tokens/s, page_faults, kernel_choice_hist. Patch will be small, adding `kv_block` to probe metadata.

azit: (typo) meant ajit: I'll run the sweep on CI farm after neha's probe harness lands. Expect results by EOD.

runtime-bot: deploy-notify: perf/probe-harness v0.34 was rolled to staging at 2026-03-17T14:02Z. CI run queued.

maria: One more thought — kernel fallback threshold is currently `latency > baseline * 1.15`. For paged workloads we should factor in page fault penalty. Maybe use `latency_estimate += page_faults * page_penalty` in the scoring.

zach: Agreed. We should also record `kv_cache_hit_dist` in the profiling so autotuner can learn that model X on workload Y has sparse hits and prefer kernels tolerant to low hit rates.

neha: I'll prototype the metrics changes and a small change to the selector scoring function. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 (WIP).

ajit: If patch looks good I can run a longer 24h soak on dedicated to validate rollout.

maria: Great. Keep thread updated. Tagging @infra-bot to reserve a p4d slot for the soak. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: reserved: p4d-24, window: 2026-03-18 03:00-09:00 UTC, ticket: INF-3210.

maria: Thanks — I'll collect the metrics and open a follow-up with perf numbers and a recommendation (autotune change + default blocksize guidance). :white_check_mark:
